name: registry.key.delete
description: Delete a registry key. Empty keys require no flags. Pass `recursive: true` to delete a key and all its subkeys.

recursive.description: If true, delete the key and all its subkeys recursively (analogous to `reg.exe DELETE /F /S`). Without this, deleting a key with subkeys returns ERR not_empty.

x-output-schema.description: Empty body — wire response is the literal `OK 0`.

x-implementations.name: reg_delete_key_ex
x-implementations.description: Win32 `RegDeleteKeyExW` for the empty-key case (NT 5.2+). Picks 32-vs-64-bit view explicitly via samDesired.

x-implementations.name: reg_delete_tree
x-implementations.description: Win32 `RegDeleteTreeW` for the recursive case (Vista+). NT 5.0/5.1/5.2 don't have RegDeleteTree; agent emulates via recursive enumeration + RegDeleteKey.

windows-modern.description: RegDeleteTreeW (Vista+) for recursive whole-key delete. Pre-Vista (NT 5.0/5.1/5.2 in modern's lineage) emulates recursive delete via RegEnumKeyExW walk + RegDeleteKeyExW. Empty-key case uses RegDeleteKeyExW directly.

windows-classic.description: RegDeleteKeyW (no Ex variant pre-NT-5.2). Recursive delete always emulated via enumeration. Win 9x lacks SeRestorePrivilege gating; classic agent's permission errors map to ERR permission_denied uniformly.
